specStatements.text: Plants produce hormones to coordinate and control growth and responses to light (phototropism) and gravity (gravitropism or geotropism). Unequal distributions of auxin cause unequal growth rates in plant roots and shoots.
Gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination.
Ethene controls cell division and ripening of fruits.
The mechanisms of how gibberellins and ethene work are not required.
Students should be able to describe the effects of some plant hormones and the different ways people use them to control plant growth.
Plant growth hormones are used in agriculture and horticulture.
Auxins are used: as weed killers; as rooting powders; for promoting growth in tissue culture.
Ethene is used in the food industry to control ripening of fruit during storage and transport.
Gibberellins can be used to: end seed dormancy; promote flowering; increase fruit size.

scopeNotes.statement: The mechanisms of how gibberellins and ethene work are not required.
scopeNotes.howHonoured: The mechanisms of how gibberellins and ethene work are not required, so gibberellins and ethene are treated only as named hormones with stated effects (initiating seed germination; controlling cell division and ripening of fruits) and stated commercial uses. No concept, misconception or question asks how either hormone acts inside the plant, and no cellular or molecular detail is given for them.

concepts.definition: A chemical produced by a plant that coordinates and controls growth and the plant's responses to stimuli such as light and gravity.
The growth response of a plant to light. A shoot lit from one side bends towards the light because auxin is unequally distributed, giving unequal growth rates on the two sides.
The growth response of a plant to gravity. Roots grow towards gravity and shoots grow away from it, because auxin is unequally distributed and causes unequal growth rates.

A plant hormone whose unequal distribution causes unequal growth rates in plant roots and shoots. Where auxin collects in a shoot the growth rate increases; where it collects in a root the growth rate is reduced, so the shoot or root bends.
Plant hormones that are important in initiating seed germination.
A plant hormone that controls cell division and the ripening of fruits.

concepts.term: Commercial use of plant growth hormones
concepts.definition: Plant growth hormones are used in agriculture and horticulture to control plant growth: auxins as weed killers, as rooting powders and for promoting growth in tissue culture; ethene in the food industry to control ripening of fruit during storage and transport; gibberellins to end seed dormancy, promote flowering and increase fruit size.

misconceptions.question: In a shoot lit from one side, on which side does auxin collect?
misconceptions.correct: On the shaded side, where the extra auxin increases the growth rate so the shoot bends towards the light.
misconceptions.misconception: Auxin is drawn towards the light, so it collects on the lit side of the shoot.
misconceptions.whyItArises: Students see the shoot bend towards the light and assume the hormone must move towards the light as well; textbook diagrams often shade one side without labelling where the auxin has gone.
misconceptions.correction: Unequal distribution of auxin places more auxin on the shaded side of the shoot. That side grows faster, so the shoot bends towards the light (phototropism).

misconceptions.question: Does more auxin always give a faster growth rate?
misconceptions.correct: No. More auxin increases the growth rate in a shoot but reduces the growth rate in a root.
misconceptions.misconception: Auxin speeds up growth wherever it collects, in roots just as it does in shoots.
misconceptions.whyItArises: Auxin is first met as the hormone that makes shoots grow towards light, so students carry that single effect across to roots without checking it.
misconceptions.correction: Unequal distributions of auxin cause unequal growth rates in plant roots and shoots. In a root the side with more auxin grows less, so the root bends towards gravity (gravitropism).

misconceptions.question: Which hormone initiates seed germination and which one ripens fruit?
misconceptions.correct: Gibberellins initiate seed germination; ethene controls cell division and the ripening of fruits.
misconceptions.misconception: Ethene is the hormone that starts seeds germinating and gibberellins are the hormone that ripens fruit.
misconceptions.whyItArises: The two hormones are met together in one short section and both are linked to seeds and fruit, so the names get swapped.
misconceptions.correction: Gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination. Ethene controls cell division and ripening of fruits.

misconceptions.question: Can a weed killer containing auxins be sprayed on a growing cereal crop?
misconceptions.correct: Yes. The weed killer disturbs the growth of the weeds so that they die, while the cereal crop keeps growing.
misconceptions.misconception: A weed killer containing auxins kills every plant it is sprayed on, so it cannot be used on a crop.
misconceptions.whyItArises: Students think of weed killers as general poisons and do not expect a plant growth hormone to affect the weeds but not the crop.
misconceptions.correction: Auxins are used as weed killers in agriculture and horticulture. They upset the growth of the weeds, which die, while the crop plants are unaffected and grow on.

misconceptions.question: How is ethene used to control the ripening of fruit during storage and transport?
misconceptions.correct: Fruit is picked and transported unripe, and ethene is used to start it ripening at the right time.
misconceptions.misconception: Ethene is added to fruit to stop it ripening while it is being stored and transported.
misconceptions.whyItArises: Students know that fruit arrives in the shops unripe, so they assume the chemical that is added must be what is holding the ripening back.
misconceptions.correction: Ethene is used in the food industry to control ripening of fruit during storage and transport: it is used to bring on ripening, so ripening happens when the grower or seller wants it.

misconceptions.question: What is the effect of treating dormant seeds with gibberellins?
misconceptions.correct: The dormancy is ended, so the seeds are able to germinate.
misconceptions.misconception: Gibberellins are used to keep seeds dormant so that they can be stored for longer.
misconceptions.whyItArises: The phrase 'used to end seed dormancy' is read as 'used for seed dormancy', and students associate any treatment of seeds with keeping them in storage.
misconceptions.correction: Gibberellins can be used to end seed dormancy, promote flowering and increase fruit size.

mcqs.stem: A young shoot is lit from one side only and bends towards the light. Which explains this?

options.text: Auxin gathers on the lit side, which grows faster.
options.rationale: A student who believes auxin is drawn towards the light expects the extra auxin on the lit side. In fact the unequal distribution of auxin places more auxin on the shaded side, so it is the shaded side that grows faster.

options.text: Auxin gathers on the shaded side, which grows less.
options.rationale: A student who thinks auxin holds growth back wherever it collects picks the slower option. Auxin reduces the growth rate in a root, but in a shoot the side with more auxin grows faster.

options.text: Auxin gathers on the shaded side, which grows faster.
options.rationale: Unequal distribution of auxin gives more auxin on the shaded side of the shoot, which produces a faster growth rate on that side, so the shoot bends towards the light (phototropism).

options.text: Auxin gathers on the lit side, which then grows slower.
options.rationale: A student who believes auxin moves towards the light places it on the lit side and then has to slow that side down to get the bend. Auxin collects on the shaded side and speeds growth there.

mcqs.stem: A seedling is laid on its side in the dark. Which describes the response of its root?

options.text: Auxin gathers on the lower side, which grows more quickly.
options.rationale: A student who thinks more auxin always means faster growth picks this. In a root the side with more auxin grows less, which is why the root bends downwards towards gravity.

options.text: Auxin collects on the upper side, which grows slower.
options.rationale: A student who believes auxin moves away from the ground, in the way they think it moves towards light in a shoot, expects it on the upper side. Gravity gives an unequal distribution with more auxin on the lower side of the root.

options.text: Auxin gathers on the lower side, which grows slower.
options.rationale: Unequal distribution of auxin gives more auxin on the lower side of the root, where it causes a slower growth rate, so the root bends downwards (gravitropism or geotropism).

options.text: Auxin gathers on the upper side, which then grows faster.
options.rationale: This combines auxin on the wrong side with the idea that auxin always speeds growth; it would bend the root upwards. Auxin collects on the lower side and reduces growth there.

mcqs.stem: Which effect of a plant hormone is described correctly?

options.text: Gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination.
options.rationale: This is the stated effect of gibberellins: they are important in initiating seed germination.

options.text: Ethene is important in initiating germination of seeds.
options.rationale: A student who has swapped the two hormones gives germination to ethene. Ethene controls cell division and ripening of fruits; gibberellins initiate seed germination.

options.text: Gibberellins are important in maintaining seed dormancy.
options.rationale: A student who reads 'end seed dormancy' as 'cause seed dormancy' picks this. Gibberellins can be used to end seed dormancy, not to maintain it.

options.text: Ethene is important in preventing the ripening of fruits.
options.rationale: A student who thinks ethene is added to hold fruit back picks this. Ethene controls cell division and ripening of fruits, and is used to bring ripening on.

mcqs.stem: A farmer sprays a field of cereal plants with a weed killer containing auxins. What is the result?

options.text: The weeds and the cereal crop are both killed off.
options.rationale: A student who treats an auxin weed killer as a general poison expects everything sprayed to die. Auxin weed killers upset the growth of the weeds while the crop grows on.

options.text: The weeds and the cereal crop both grow faster now.
options.rationale: A student who thinks auxin always speeds growth up expects extra growth all round. Auxins used as weed killers disturb the growth of the weeds so that they die.

options.text: The cereal dies and the weeds keep on growing.
options.rationale: A student who thinks the spray kills any plant it lands on may pick the crop as the victim. The weed killer kills the weeds; the cereal crop continues to grow.

options.text: The weeds die and the cereal crop keeps growing.
options.rationale: Auxins are used as weed killers in agriculture: the hormone upsets the growth of the weeds so that they die, while the cereal crop is unaffected.

mcqs.stem: Bananas are picked unripe and kept cool while they are shipped. Ethene is used on them when they arrive. Why?

options.text: To stop the fruit from ripening while it is stored.
options.rationale: A student who thinks ethene is a preservative picks this. Ethene controls ripening by bringing it on, so it is used at the end of storage and transport, not to prevent ripening.

options.text: To start the fruit ripening at the end of storage.
options.rationale: Ethene controls the ripening of fruits and is used in the food industry to control ripening during storage and transport, so the fruit ripens when it is wanted.

options.text: To keep the fruit firm until it is in the shops.
options.rationale: Keeping the fruit firm is achieved by picking it unripe and keeping it cool, not by ethene. Ethene is the hormone that controls ripening of the fruit.

options.text: To make the seeds inside the fruit start growing.
options.rationale: A student who has swapped the hormones expects ethene to act on seeds. Gibberellins are important in initiating seed germination; ethene controls ripening of fruits.

mcqs.stem: A grower treats a fruit crop with gibberellins. Which result would be expected?

options.text: The fruits ripen early, before reaching full size.
options.rationale: A student who thinks gibberellins ripen fruit picks early ripening. Ripening is controlled by ethene; gibberellins can be used to increase fruit size.

options.text: The seeds inside the fruits are kept in dormancy.
options.rationale: A student who links gibberellins with causing dormancy picks this. Gibberellins can be used to end seed dormancy, not to keep seeds dormant.

options.text: The treated plants are killed off by the spray.
options.rationale: A student who thinks any hormone spray acts as a weed killer picks this. Auxins are used as weed killers; gibberellins are used to increase fruit size.

options.text: The fruits grow larger than untreated fruits.
options.rationale: Gibberellins can be used to increase fruit size, which is one of the ways plant growth hormones are used in agriculture and horticulture.
